title: English Vocabulary 4 · Units 41–42
description: Advanced vocabulary for UK parliamentary processes, international institutions, diplomatic discussions, political movements and international conferences.
sourceNotice: Prepared for personal study from the user-provided book. Source vocabulary, explanations and exercise answers informed the lexical selection; all card examples, Portuguese translations and explanatory notes were independently written without reproducing long passages, exercises or artwork.

audit.scope: Unit 41 and Unit 42 teaching material (including glossaries), exercises 41.1–41.5 and 42.1–42.4, and their answer key entries.
audit.pronunciation: Broad British IPA provided for selected short targets where pronunciation is sufficiently reliable; longer expressions have blank IPA. IPA is not an exhaustive connected-speech guide.
audit.languagePolicy: All learner-facing content and metadata are in English, with Brazilian Portuguese translations only under pt.
audit.reviewMethod: Compared the teaching pages and exercises with answer-key entries; reviewed collocations, UK-specific usage, grammar patterns, original examples, translations, provenance and word-audio targets; programmatically validated schema, identifiers and JSON syntax.
audit.limitations: No MP3 recordings are embedded. VocabLab browser import, live speech recognition and browser TTS output were not tested. The text reflects the book’s teaching material and is not an assertion that parliamentary procedures are unchanged since publication.

units.title: Unit 41 — British politics
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 41. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Politics · UK parliament and political participation
learningObjectives: Describe how citizens can lobby representatives, petition Parliament and submit evidence.
Distinguish MPs, peers, the House of Commons, the House of Lords and Select Committees.
Use parliamentary collocations accurately, including committee stage, briefing material and party policy.
Discuss scrutiny, allegations and the work of committees with appropriate neutral register.

sectionsChecked: A · Influencing political decisions and glossary
B · Lobbying and petitioning, including both information boxes
C · Select Committees and specialist political terms

items.pt: ter voz; poder opinar ou participar de uma decisão
items.example: Local residents deserve to have a say in decisions affecting their neighbourhood.
items.note: Often have a say in something; refers to having an opportunity to influence a decision.

items.example: Environmental groups lobbied several MPs before the debate.
items.note: Lobby someone or lobby for or against a policy; it means trying to influence decision-makers.

items.pt: parlamentar da Câmara dos Comuns; deputado britânico
items.example: The MP met residents to discuss concerns about public transport.
items.note: Member of Parliament; in this unit specifically a member of the UK House of Commons.

items.pt: membro da Câmara dos Lordes; par do Reino Unido
items.example: A peer raised the issue during a debate in the upper chamber.
items.note: In UK parliamentary language, a member of the House of Lords; not simply a colleague of equal standing.

items.pt: Câmara dos Lordes do Reino Unido
items.example: The proposal was also examined in the House of Lords.
items.note: The upper chamber of the UK Parliament; members are often called peers.

items.pt: Câmara dos Comuns do Reino Unido
items.example: The House of Commons debated the proposed reforms.
items.note: The elected lower chamber of the UK Parliament.

items.example: Residents petitioned Parliament to reconsider the transport plan.
items.note: Both a noun and a verb; a petition formally asks an authority to act or consider a matter.

items.pt: legislação; conjunto de leis ou propostas legislativas
items.example: New legislation was proposed to strengthen consumer protection.
items.note: Uncountable when referring to laws collectively; proposed legislation may not yet be law.

items.pt: fase de análise detalhada em comissão parlamentar
items.example: The bill received detailed scrutiny during the committee stage.
items.note: A stage of the UK legislative process when a bill is examined in detail.

items.pt: projeto de lei de interesse público no Parlamento britânico
items.example: The Public Bill was referred for further consideration.
items.note: A UK parliamentary bill concerning a matter of public policy, as distinct from a Private Bill.

items.example: Several specialists were invited to submit evidence to the inquiry.
items.note: Submit evidence to a committee or inquiry; evidence can include testimony, documents and research.

items.pt: comissão parlamentar de fiscalização e investigação
items.example: A Select Committee questioned officials about the department’s spending.
items.note: A parliamentary committee that investigates or scrutinises a defined area.

items.example: The committee will scrutinise the proposed budget in detail.
items.note: More exacting than simply look at; British spelling scrutinise, American scrutinize.

items.pt: atuação de lobby; pressão sobre representantes políticos
items.example: The organisation disclosed its lobbying activities in the annual report.
items.note: Noun for activities intended to influence public policy or officials.

items.pt: material informativo para orientar uma decisão
items.example: The adviser prepared briefing material before the ministerial meeting.
items.note: Briefing is the provision of essential background information; common in government and business.

items.example: Supporters gathered at a rally outside the city hall.
items.note: A public meeting or demonstration intended to express support or opposition.

items.pt: em última análise; no fim das contas
items.example: Ultimately, the committee members had to make their own decision.
items.note: Signals the final determining factor after considering other issues.

items.example: Whether to approve the amendment is down to the elected representatives.
items.note: In this sense, the decision is down to somebody; it means they are responsible for it.

items.pt: posição ou diretriz oficial de um partido político
items.example: Her comments did not reflect the party policy on housing.
items.note: The policy adopted by a political party; distinguish it from an MP’s personal view.

items.pt: informar alguém sobre; conscientizar alguém de
items.example: The campaign aims to make voters aware of the proposed changes.
items.note: Common pattern: make someone aware of something.
items.speechText: make voters aware of the changes

items.pt: apresentar em formato definido; organizar por escrito
items.example: The applicants set out their requests clearly in the letter.
items.note: In the petition context, be properly set out means be written in the required format; set out also means explain in detail.

items.example: A local campaign launched an e-petition calling for safer roads.
items.note: An electronic petition; no universal signature threshold is implied.

items.pt: registro oficial dos debates parlamentares britânicos
items.example: The researcher checked Hansard for the wording of the speech.
items.note: The official record of parliamentary proceedings in the United Kingdom.

items.example: The representative agreed to present a petition on behalf of residents.
items.note: Present means formally submit or make known in a parliamentary setting, not give a gift.

items.pt: eleitor ou morador de uma circunscrição eleitoral
items.example: The MP answered questions from a constituent about local services.
items.note: A constituent lives or votes in an elected representative’s constituency.

items.pt: circunscrição eleitoral; distrito representado por um parlamentar
items.example: She returned to her constituency to meet community leaders.
items.note: The geographical area represented by an elected MP; do not confuse with a political party.

items.pt: presidente da Câmara dos Comuns britânica
items.example: The Speaker called the next MP to speak during the debate.
items.note: In the House of Commons, the presiding officer responsible for maintaining parliamentary procedure.

items.pt: plenário; sala onde ocorrem debates parlamentares
items.example: The minister entered the debating chamber before the session began.
items.note: In the source, the place where parliamentary discussions take place.

items.example: The department was invited to offer observations on the petition.
items.note: Formal administrative phrasing; observations here means considered comments, not visual sightings.

items.example: The committee asked for a substantive reply rather than a brief acknowledgement.
items.note: Describes something important in content or substance, as opposed to merely procedural.

items.example: The government department released a report on its spending.
items.note: In British politics, a department is an administrative branch responsible for a policy area.

items.example: The inquiry examined both policy decisions and day-to-day administration.
items.note: Here it refers to how government work is managed; elsewhere it can mean a governing team.

items.example: The review crosses departmental boundaries because it involves transport and energy.
items.note: Used when an issue spans the responsibilities of more than one government department.

items.pt: auditoria ou avaliação de impactos ambientais
items.example: The committee requested an environmental audit of the proposed development.
items.note: Audit suggests systematic scrutiny rather than a casual inspection.

items.pt: alegação de irregularidade ainda não comprovada
items.example: An independent inquiry examined allegations of misconduct.
items.note: An allegation is a claim that has not necessarily been proved.

items.example: Questions were raised about the official’s conduct during the inquiry.
items.note: Noun pronounced with first-syllable stress; the verb conduct has different stress.

items.pt: acompanhar e fiscalizar de perto a atuação de
items.example: The committee shadows the department’s work and reviews major decisions.
items.note: In this political sense, follow the work of a department closely; not a literal shadow.

items.example: The panel drew on the wide-ranging expertise of its members.
items.note: Wide-ranging describes a breadth of areas; expertise refers to deep knowledge or skill.

items.pt: constituição; conjunto de princípios e normas fundamentais de um país
items.example: The report considered whether the proposal was compatible with the constitution.
items.note: The source refers to the UK constitution; constitutional arrangements differ across countries.

items.example: The committee inquiry gathered evidence from several independent witnesses.
items.note: An inquiry seeks evidence on an issue; often followed by into a matter.

items.pt: cadeira da presidência da Câmara dos Comuns
items.example: The guide pointed towards the Speaker’s Chair during the visit.
items.note: UK-specific parliamentary term also reinforced in the unit’s collocation exercise.

units.title: Unit 42 — International politics
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 42. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Use vocabulary for the aims and work of the United Nations and diplomatic negotiation.
Describe political movements, integration, liberation, demonstrations and solidarity.
Explain conference aims and international policy using appropriate formal collocations.
Recognise verb-noun families in word formation exercises, including justify/justification and negotiate/negotiation.

sectionsChecked: A · United Nations with annotated definitions
C · International conferences with annotated definitions

items.example: The United Nations hosted talks on humanitarian cooperation.
items.note: The UN is an international organisation established in 1945.

items.example: The members constituted a formal association to coordinate their work.
items.note: Formal verb for establishing a body; distinguish from constitute meaning amount to.

items.example: The appeal emphasised our shared responsibility to humanity.
items.note: Here humanity means humankind, not simply kindness or compassion.

items.example: The institution expanded rapidly after its foundation.
items.note: In this context foundation is the establishment of an organisation; it can also mean a base.

items.example: The coalition continued to pursue its goal of expanding access to education.
items.note: Pursue commonly collocates with an aim, goal, career or strategy.

items.example: The two countries sought to establish friendly relations after years of tension.
items.note: Establish means create or set in place; relations is normally plural in this diplomatic sense.

items.example: The initiative aims to conquer poverty through long-term investment.
items.note: Figurative conquer means overcome; not military conquest in this context.

items.example: The charity developed programmes aimed at reducing illiteracy.
items.note: The inability to read or write; contrast with literacy.

items.pt: negociação; tentativa de chegar a um acordo
items.example: Successful negotiation requires trust and a willingness to compromise.
items.note: Often plural negotiations when referring to a series of formal talks.

items.example: The campaign called attention to injustice in access to housing.
items.note: May describe a specific unfair act or a broader unfair state of affairs.

items.pt: defender; garantir o respeito a direitos
items.example: Independent institutions have a duty to uphold fundamental rights.
items.note: Uphold a right, principle, law or decision means support or maintain it.

items.example: The policy was criticised for excluding a linguistic minority.
items.note: May refer to an ethnic, religious or other smaller group; distinguish numerical and political senses.

items.example: The report examined barriers faced by members of an ethnic minority.
items.note: Ethnic minority is a common collocation; avoid implying a single shared identity or experience.

items.example: Diplomats debated whether military intervention could be justified.
items.note: Military involvement in a conflict or crisis; the context determines the legal and political assessment.

items.example: The minister was asked to justify the proposed expenditure.
items.note: Justify an action means provide an adequate reason; justification is the noun.

items.example: The political movement campaigned for expanded voting rights.
items.note: A group organised around shared political beliefs or objectives.

items.example: The campaign adopted a memorable slogan for its posters.
items.note: A short, memorable phrase intended to communicate a message.

items.example: The movement described equal rights as central to liberation.
items.note: Noun related to liberate; often used in political or social contexts.

items.pt: integração; inclusão em um grupo ou sociedade
items.example: The programme supported the integration of newly arrived families.
items.note: Integration into a society or community involves participation and inclusion.

items.pt: ser excluído de; ficar de fora de
items.example: Some residents felt they had been excluded from the consultation process.
items.note: The usual pattern is be excluded from something.

items.pt: participar de uma marcha ou manifestação
items.example: Students decided to go on a march in support of education funding.
items.note: A march is an organised public demonstration; go on a march is a fixed expression.

items.pt: solidariedade; união em apoio a uma causa
items.example: The workers expressed solidarity with colleagues facing redundancy.
items.note: Often show or express solidarity with somebody.

items.example: Delegates attended an international conference on energy security.
items.note: A formal gathering of participants from different countries.

items.example: Each participating organisation nominated a delegate to the meeting.
items.note: Noun: a person authorised to represent a group; verb delegate is pronounced differently.

items.example: The working group will determine which proposals are feasible.
items.note: Formal verb meaning decide, establish or discover on the basis of evidence.

items.example: The engineers redesigned the system to minimise energy losses.
items.note: British spelling minimise; American minimize; often minimise risk, damage or consumption.

items.example: The new facility has lower energy requirements than the old one.
items.note: Requirements here means what is needed to operate a system.

items.example: Reliable infrastructure is essential for public transport and sanitation.
items.note: The basic physical and organisational systems needed by a society.

items.pt: com o objetivo de; visando a
items.example: The committee met with a view to reaching an agreement before Friday.
items.note: Formal: with a view to + noun or -ing, not with a view to reach.

items.example: The conference discussed measures designed to slow global warming.
items.note: Long-term rise in average global temperature; the unit treats it as an international policy issue.

items.example: Both sides recognise the importance of clear communication.
items.note: Follow recognise the importance of with a noun or -ing form.

items.pt: comprometer-se a; assumir o compromisso de
items.example: The signatories undertook to publish regular progress reports.
items.note: Formal undertake to + infinitive means promise or commit oneself to do something.

items.pt: conjunto organizado de medidas; programa de ações
items.example: The ministers proposed a programme of measures to protect water supplies.
items.note: In policy writing, programme means an organised series of actions; British spelling.

items.example: The proposed reforms are undeniably ambitious.
items.note: Adverb expressing a strong claim that something cannot reasonably be denied.

items.pt: delicado; que exige tato e cuidado
items.example: The mediator handled the delicate question of border access carefully.
items.note: In diplomacy, delicate describes an issue requiring sensitive treatment, not something physically fragile.

items.example: The coalition struggled to maintain unity during the negotiations.
items.note: A state of acting together; related to unite.

items.example: It is customary to circulate the agenda before the meeting.
items.note: Typical or usual in a given setting; it is customary to + infinitive.

items.pt: constituição; conjunto de regras fundamentais de uma organização ou país
items.example: The association revised its constitution to clarify voting rights.
items.note: Noun associated with constitute; can refer to a formal body’s governing rules.

items.example: Several academics founded an institute for public policy research.
items.note: Verb found means establish; do not confuse with past tense found of find.

items.example: The founder described why the organisation was created.
items.note: Person noun derived from found; contrasts with foundation, the event or institution.

items.example: The agreement included an undertaking to provide financial support.
items.note: Noun related to undertake; can refer to a promise or a substantial task.

items.example: The chief negotiator proposed a revised timetable.
items.note: Person who conducts negotiations.

items.example: The committee requested a detailed justification for the decision.
items.note: Noun related to justify; frequently justification for something.

items.example: The historian described the conquest of the territory.
items.note: A conquest usually concerns gaining control, often by force; different from figurative conquer poverty.

items.example: The museum displayed accounts written by the conquerors.
items.note: Person noun derived from conquer, usually in historical contexts.

items.example: The campaign sought to liberate people from oppressive restrictions.
items.note: Related to liberation; pattern liberate someone from something.

items.example: Supporters hailed the leader as a liberator.
items.note: A person regarded as freeing others from oppression or control.

items.pt: unir; juntar em torno de um objetivo
items.example: The initiative helped unite several community organisations.
items.note: Verb related to unity; unite groups, or unite behind a shared purpose.

items.example: A delegation from the university visited the international summit.
items.note: A group of delegates; the word can also mean assigning tasks to others.

items.example: The treaty received formal recognition from several states.
items.note: Noun related to recognise; can mean official acknowledgement or personal appreciation.

items.example: The community developed a more integrated public transport network.
items.note: Related to integrate and integration; can describe cohesive systems or societies.
